newsitem.title: USA: Clinton chooses Jane Garvey to head FAA.
newsitem.headline: Clinton chooses Jane Garvey to head FAA.

text.p: President Clinton plans to nominate Jane Garvey, a former director of Boston's busy Logan Airport, to head the Federal Aviation Administration, a senior administration official said Tuesday.

Garvey, acting head of the Federal Highway Administration, would succeed David Hinson to lead the agency that oversees the U.S. air tranportation system. The post has been vacant since Hinson, a former commercial pilot and airline executive, retired in November after serving more than three years.

During Hinson's tenure, the FAA came under sharp criticism after the crash last May 11 of ValuJet flight 592 near Miami, killing all 110 people on board. The FAA, blamed for lax oversight of the fast-growing airline, later increased oversight of start-up carriers.

Garvey's nomination would break the tradition of pilots being named as FAA administrator. But she would come with the experience of having been a director of Boston's Logan International Airport, one of the busiest in the nation, before being named FHA deputy administator under Administrator Rodney Slater.
Slater is now Secretary of Transportation, overseeing both the FAA and the FHA.
From 1988-91, Garvey was commissioner of the Massachusetts Department of Public Works, and before that she was an associate commissioner in the department.

It was not immediately clear what kind of reception Garvey would get from the aviation community, many of whose leaders had sought someone with more hands-on experience in the industry and special expertise on safety.

Industry officials have also said a new FAA head should have a technical background to oversee the expansion of the agency's highly automated air traffic control system that is needed to cope with the increasingly crowded U.S. skies.
But it seemed clear the White House would not be ready to nominate her without assurances of Senate confirmation.
